original_evidence:
Erhaltene Artikulation im rechten Kniegelenk. Als anatomische Normvariante Patella tripartita am superolateralen Pol (4/7) mit geringem Knochenmarködem in dem kleinerem akzessorischen Fragment (4/7). Ansonsten altersentsprechendes Knochenmarkssignal.

Patella zentriert stehend. Mehrere oberflächliche, teils bis zur Hälfte der Knorpelschicht erreichenden chondralen Läsionen (siehe z. B. 7/9). Chondrale Calcinosis femoropatellar, führend retropatellar (z. B. 3/46 und 3/57). Ansonsten erhaltene Knorpelbelag.

Femorotibial lateralseitig erhaltener Knorpelbelag ohne tief greifende Chondropathie jedoch mit auffallender chondraler Calcinosis (z. B. 4/25). Der Außenmeniskus ist intakt.

Medialseitig teils fokal tief greifende Chondropathie (z. B. 6/10 oder 4/23) in der Hauptbelastungszone der Femurkondyle. Ansonsten vorwiegend oberflächliche Chondropathie. Hier nur sehr geringe Chondrokalzinose. Der Innenmeniskus ab Pars intermedia bis ins Hinterhorn deutlich signalalteriert und aufgetrieben mit schräger Risskomponente (z. B. 5/9) und kleiner meniscealer Zyste (4/19). Diskrete osteophytäre Anbauten (1005/73).

Vorderes und hinteres Kreuzband intakt. Kollateralbänder intakt, geringer Reizzustand des MCL. Geringer Gelenkerguss. Synovialis nicht verdickt. Vergrößerte Bursa praepatellaris (5/20). Ansonsten unauffällige Darstellung der umgebenden Muskulatur und der Subkutis.

original_evidence:
MRI of right Knee with 
-SG PD FatSat, Locator, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS, Sag T2W STIR, AX T2W STIR



> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus and anterior horn of lateral meniscus, with extending into the surface, R/O tear.
> The contour of ACL, PCL and MCL is in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside on T1WI and F/S T2WI, R/O grade 1 injury.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> A lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst, about 5.7 cm in length.
> Wearing of articular cartilage and subchondral bone marrow edema and tiny subchondral cyst of right knee, more prominent at medial femoral conylde and tibial plateau; spur formation also noted.. 
> Some circumscribed abnormal bone marrow signal foci in right distal femur with hypointensity lines, major at epimetaphysis, R/O bone infarcts.
> Varocise veins, more prominent at lateral side.

Impression: 
1. C/W osteoarthritis of right knee joint, more severe at medial compartment.
2. Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus and R/O tear of anterior horn of lateral meniscus.
3. R/O grade 1 injury or degeneration of ACL, PCL and MCL.
4. Synovitis of right knee with suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae.
5. Baker's cyst.
6. R/O small bone infarcts of right dital femur.
7. Varicose veins.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

original_evidence:
No significant knee effusion, there are no intra-articular bodies either.  
Multilocular cystic mass posterior to the posterior cruciate ligament, deep to the popliteal neurovascular bundle, in keeping with a ganglion cyst that is arising from the knee joint proper.
There is a complex, undisplaced tear through the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. 
There is associated high signal within the subchondral bone of the lateral aspect of the medial tibial plateau, potentially representative of a bone marrow contusion. 
Any history of direct trauma to account for such appearances?
The lateral meniscus is intact, as are the cruciate and collateral ligaments, distal iliotibial band, popliteus musculotendinous unit, extensor tendons in the remaining marrow signal throughout.
High-riding patella noted, together with pre femoral fat pad impingement - any history of anterior knee pain?
Solitary grade 3 cartilage fissure noted at the medial retropatellar facet.
Tricompartmental articular cartilage is otherwise well preserved.  
Anterior subcutaneous edema like signal change with no discrete bursal formation, kindly correlate clinically.
Grossly unremarkable remaining imaged extra-articular soft tissues. 

Impression:
Complex undisplaced medial meniscal tear.
Focal medial retropatellar cartilage damage.
Multifactorial low grade extensor mechanism pathology.
Suspected posteromedial proximal tibial bone marrow contusion.

original_evidence:
Antecedentes Clínicos:
Sospecha lesión meniscal.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colateral lateral sin alteraciones. Leve engrosamiento impresiona secuelar
del tercio proximal del componente superficial del ligamento colateral medial. El resto de sus
componentes sin alteraciones significativas.
Menisco lateral de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Rotura horizontal oblicua del cuerno posterior y cuerpo del menisco medial con segmento
parcialmente desplazado hacia región intercondílea posterior. Esto se asocia discreta extrusión
meniscal y discreto edema las partes blandas adyacentes.
Condropatía superficial de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial. El
resto de los cartílagos femorotibiales y patelofemoral sin alteraciones.
Leve derrame articular. Pequeño quiste poplíteo no complicado.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial
dentro de límites normales.
Discreto edema de las partes blandas entre la banda iliotibial y el cóndilo femoral lateral.
Impresión:
Leve engrosamiento secuelar del tercio proximal del componente superficial del ligamento
colateral medial.
Rotura del menisco medial con segmento parcialmente desplazado hacia la región intercondílea
posterior.
Condropatía superficial de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial.
Leve derrame articular. Pequeño quiste poplíteo no complicado.
Probables fenómenos de fricción de la banda iliotibial

Moderate degenerative change.
Complex degenerative tear with a dominant longitudinal horizontal oblique component of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with inferior surfacing. Fraying and blunting of the meniscal free edge.

Diffuse low grade partial-thickness chondral loss. Marginal osteophytosis.

Thickened popliteus insertion with intrasubstance signal compatible with moderate tendinosis
Mildly thickened lateral collateral ligament proper which could reflect the sequela of a remote injury. Mild distal biceps tendinosis.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Degenerative changes of the anterior cruciate ligament which remains intact. The PCL is intact.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):

Scarring at that the Hoffa's fat pad which could reflect the previous surgery-for clinical correlation.

Bones:
See above.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
The intra-articular body is seen at the suprapatellar joint recess on the previous MRI is no longer present.

3.Mild degenerative change of the patellofemoral compartment.

original_evidence:
LEFT KNEE MRI 

CLINICAL INDICATION: Medial meniscus injury, query MCL tear

Technique: Multiplanar PD, PF fat sat and T1 imaging was acquired through the knee. 

Comparison: The x-ray [Date]

Findings:

General:
Marrow:  There is edema of the medial femoral condyle at the site of the MCL insertion, and in the posterolateral femoral condyle. There is edema in the medial proximal tibia and the posterolateral proximal tibia.
Consistent with internal bone contusion secondary valgus injury.
Effusion:  No significant effusion

Menisci:   
Medial meniscus:   Intact.
Lateral meniscus:   Intact.

Ligaments and tendons:
Cruciate ligaments:   There is increased signal in the PCL, which may be keeping with a low-grade tear. No tibial translation.
Medial collateral ligament:   High-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal of the mid fibers of the superficial medial collateral ligament. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the meniscal femoral as well as posterior plate components of the deep medial collateral ligament.
Lateral collateral ligament:   normal
Popliteofibular ligament:   normal
Other posterolateral corner ligaments:   normal
Popliteal tendon:   normal
Iliotibial band:   normal

Extensor mechanism:
Quadriceps tendon: Mild increased signal along the patellar insertion, in keeping with tendinosis
Patella:   normal
Patellar tendon:   normal
Hoffa?s fat pad: Subtle edema in keeping with impingement

Cartilage:
Patellofemoral joint: Mild chondrosis mainly along the trochlear aspect there
Medial compartment:   normal cartilage
Lateral compartment:  Mild chondrosis.

CONCLUSION:

1. Intact menisci.
2. High-grade partial thickness tear of the medial collateral ligament and bone contusions posterior lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau in keeping with valgus injury.
3. Mild chondrosis.
4. Mild quadriceps tendinosis without tear.

original_evidence:
Constatations:

Épanchement intra-articulaire modéré, avec suspicion d'un niveau graisseux au versant externe suggérant un degré de lipohémarthrose. Pas de kyste de Baker significatif avec un liséré de liquide au sein du creux poplité et de la portion supérieure de la patte d'oie. 

Il y a un émoussement du rebord postérieur de la corne postérieure du ménisque interne suspect d'une déchirure longitudinale verticale périphérique potentielle. Il y a également une extrusion relativement significative du corps méniscal, le plus probablement en lien avec une déchirure complète du ligament collatéral interne. 

Il y a une déchirure complète du ligament colléral interne distal avec rétraction proximale des fibres déchirées, associées à de multiples zones d'irrégularités, épaississements et signal anormal intra-substance. Il y également une atténuation et signal intra-substance à son origine. La partie distale du ligament collatéral interne déchirée se situe légèrement sous les tendons de la patte d'oie constituant une lésion de type ''pseudo Stener''. Il y a également une déchire complète de la composante profonde ménisco-fémorale et une déchirure partielle de la composante ménisco-tibiale. 

Pas d'atteinte chondrale transfixiante fémorotibiale interne.

Le ménisque externe est intact sans déchirure. Il y a une petite fracture au versant supérieur de la tête du péroné potentiellement à l'insertion du ligament poplité arqué. Minime déplacement et œdème associés. L'insertion distale du ligament collatéral externe et du tendon du biceps est préservé de même que l'origine. Il y a également une petite ossification au versant postérieur de la tête du péroné mesurant 5 mm, d'origine indéterminée. 

Il y a des irrégularités de l'os sous-chondral à la surface portante du condyle fémoral externe d'allure plutôt chronique. Pas d'atteinte chondrale transfixiante fémorotibiale externe. Toutefois, petit foyer d'œdème au versant postérieur du condyle fémoral externe avec léger hypersignal chondral, contusion versus lésion oséto-chondrale (atypique) versus changement de stress en lien avec l’origine du gastrocnémien externe. 

Kyste ganglionnaire à l'origine des deux gastrocnémiens.

Il y a une déchirure d'allure complète à l'insertion distale du ligament croisé postérieur et/ou avulsion du LCP. Le ligament est rétracté proximalement, épaissi et de signal anormal. Il y a une atténuation significative du ligament croisé antérieur sans composante transfixiante toutefois notée, en lien avec une déchirure partielle. Il y a des contusions probablement associées au plateau tibial externe, plus marquées en postérieur +/- impaction/fracture sous-chondrale.

Petit kyste ganglionnaire à l'empreinte distale du ligament croisé antérieur.

L'alignement patello-fémoral demeure dans les limites normales. Séquelles de maladie Osgood Schlatter avec fragmentation d'allure chronique de la tubérosité tibiale et léger épaississement du tendon rotulien. Le tendon du quadriceps distal est intact sans déchirure. Pas d'atteinte chondrale transfixiante patello-fémorale. La graisse de Hoffa est sans grande particularité.

Il y a un œdème diffus significatif sous-cutané et inter-musculaire. Il y a également un œdème des muscles poplité et plantaire en lien avec une entorse.

Conclusion:

Déchirure complète du ligament collatéral interne distal avec déplacement de la portion distale sous les tendons de la patte d'oie en lien avec une lésion de type 'pseudo Stener''. Il y a également une déchirure complète de la composante profonde ménisco-fémorale et partielle de la composante ménisco-tibiale.

Déchirure d'allure complète du ligament croisé postérieur distal et/ou avulsion du LCP. Déchirure partielle probable du ligament croisé antérieur.

Fracture au versant supérieur de la tête du péroné probablement à l'insertion du ligament poplité arqué. Œdème associé.

De plus, contusions probable du plateau tibial externe +/- impaction/fracture sous-chondrale et du versant postérieur du condyle fémoral externe. 

Émoussement du rebord postérieur de la corne postérieure du ménisque interne suspect d'une déchirure longitudinale verticale périphérique potentielle.

Épanchement intra-articulaire modéré avec composante de lipohémarthrose suspectée.

Dans ce contexte, un complément d'investigation par tomodensitométrie est recommandé pour mieux évaluer les structures osseuses. De plus, une consultation en chirurgie orthopédique est également, fortement recommandée. 

Le rapport a été transcrit en priorité.

original_evidence:
Mediales Kompartiment:
Zur letzten MRT-Voruntersuchung vom [DATE] konstant Nachweis einer osteochondralen Läsion an der posteromedialen Femurcondyle nahe dem Sulcus intercondylaris über eine Ausdehnung von 6 x 8 x cc 3 mm mit größenprogredienten subchondralen Zysten (Serie 4/ Image 19). Ansonsten refegrelchtes Knochenmarksignal und intakter Knorpel. Intakter Innenmeniskus. Intaktes MCL.

Laterales Kompartiment:
Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Intakter Knorpel. Intakter Außenmeniskus. Intakes LCL.

Femoropatellares Gleitlager und Trochlea:
Regelrechtes Knochenmarksignal. Fokaler, oberflächlicher Knorpeldefekt retropatellar an der medialen Patellafacette (Serie 7/ Image 10). Kein tiefgreifender oder vollschichtiger Knorpeldefekt. Kein subchondrales Knochenödem. Regelrechte Darstellung der Quadrizeps- und Patellarsehne. Regelrechte Darstellung des Hoffa`schen Fettkörpers.

Kreuzbänder:
Intakte Kreubänder.

Muskulatur und übrige Weichteile:
Akzentuierte Gelenkflüssigkeit.

original_evidence:
FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Small joint effusion. No popliteal cyst.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Grade 3 (complete disruption) injury of the distal medial collateral ligament noted. The mid and proximal collateral ligament is thickened with intrinsic high signal abnormality. There is extensive periligamentous edema.

There is some blunting and fraying of the free edge of the body of the medial meniscus suggestive of a small radial tear or defect.

The articular cartilage is unremarkable.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
The articular cartilage is unremarkable. The lateral meniscus and lateral collateral ligament complex appear normal.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
High-grade partial, functionally complete or complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.

The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Mild diffuse chondropathy is noted with superficial fraying noted on both sides of the joint, best appreciated at the median ridge of the patellar articular cartilage and in the trochlear groove. At the lateral trochlea however, there are focal areas of high-grade fissuring and delamination.

Bones:
There is a tiny subchondral impaction fracture at the posterolateral aspect of the lateral tibial plateau with associated moderate bone marrow edema.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:

1.There is a tiny subchondral impaction fracture at the posterolateral aspect of the lateral tibial plateau.
2.Grade 3 injury of the medial collateral ligament noted with complete disruption distally.
3.High-grade partial, functionally complete or complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
4.Patellofemoral chondropathy with high-grade fissuring and delamination noted involving the lateral trochlea as detailed above.
5.There is some blunting and fraying of the free edge of the body of the medial meniscus suggestive of a small radial tear or defect.

Conclusion :

Déchirure complète du ligament croisé antérieur.

original_evidence:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Medial knee pain for one week.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Healed non-ossifying fibroma at the distal femoral metaphysis.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal. Moderate extrusion of the body without discrete tear by MRI criteria.
Medial compartment cartilage: Low-grade fissuring at the notch third of the weightbearing medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss at the lateral tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full-thickness cartilage loss with subchondral edema and cystic change at the medial patellar facet and median ridge. Full thickness fissuring of the lateral facet. Partial thickness cartilage loss with full-thickness fissuring at the central and lateral trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. Mild lateral patellar tilt. No lateral translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 11 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
High-grade patellofemoral compartment chondrosis. Low-grade medial and lateral compartments chondrosis.

ADDENDUM:
[REDACTED]

original_evidence:
COMPARISON:Plain films [Date].

CLINICAL HISTORY:Twisting injury 4 weeks prior. Suspected transient lateral patellar dislocation.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the left knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The medial meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament are intact. The fibular collateral ligament is intact. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. The iliotibial band is intact. Popliteus tendon insertion is intact.

No femoral trochlear dysplasia. No patellofemoral subluxation. The TT-TG distance measures 20 mm, above the upper limit of normal. The patellar retinacula are intact. Once again seen are well-corticated osseous fragments at the tibial tuberosity in keeping with chronic sequelae of remote prior Osgood-Schlatter's disease. Minimal marrow edema and tiny cysts are noted in the fragments. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Full-thickness cartilage denuding patellar apex and along the lateral patellar facet. Mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis. Preserved medial femorotibial articular cartilage.

Trace knee joint fluid. Small Baker's cyst. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Lateralization of the tibial tubercle, predisposing to patellofemoral maltracking/instability. No patellofemoral subluxation.
2. High-grade patellofemoral chondrosis suggesting evolving moderate patellofemoral osteoarthritis of the left knee.
3. Chronic sequelae of remote prior Osgood-Schlatter's disease, also shown previously.
4. Mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis.

FINDINGS:

Fractures:
Known mildly comminuted undisplaced avulsion fracture of the tibial tuberosity involving the distal ACL insertion, anteriorly the anterior horn root insertion of the lateral meniscus, as well as posteriorly the tibial insertion of both the posterior horn of medial and lateral menisci. The fracture involves the central portion of the medial tibial plateau articular surface anteriorly and posteriorly with articular surface collapse of 3 mm anteriorly and 5 mm posteriorly, as well as a step deformity of up to 2 mm posteriorly.
Small mildly displaced avulsion fracture of the lateral corner of lateral tibial plateau [Segond fracture].
Small mild osteochondral impaction at the anterior lateral weightbearing aspect of lateral femoral condyle.
There is associated bone marrow edema associated with these fractures.

Joint alignment:
Mild widening of the medial femorotibial joint space. Otherwise preserved articular alignment.

Degenerative changes:
None.

Bone marrow signal:
Additional small area of bone marrow edema on the medial side of medial femoral condyle without evidence of associated fracture.

Anterior cruciate ligament: The distal bony avulsion with laxity of the ACL, showing some internal high T2 signal changes compatible with additional low-grade partial ligamentous tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament: Intact with mild laxity.
Medial collateral ligament: Complete tear of the superficial portion at the mid to distal third. Moderate grade partial tear of the deep meniscal femoral and meniscal tibial components with partial meniscocapsular separation of the medial meniscal body.
Lateral collateral ligament complex: Low-grade sprain of the proximal lateral collateral ligament. The other associated structures are intact.

Medial meniscus: Mild nonspecific signal changes of the meniscal body, with evidence of small horizontal oblique tear extending to the femoral surface. No other significant tear. Bony avulsion of the posterior horn root insertion as detailed above.
Lateral meniscus: Mild nonspecific signal changes at the anterior horn compatible with low-grade tearing. Evidence of small Wrisberg rip-type longitudinal tear of the periphery of the posterior horn. Complete tear of the inferior meniscal popliteal fascicle compatible with posterior lateral corner injury. There is a bony avulsion of the anterior horn and posterior horn root insertion sites.

Extensor tendons: Normal.
Patellar retinacula: Moderate grade partial tear of the medial retinaculum.
Pes anserinus: Normal.

Posteromedial and posterolateral corner: Diffuse signal change and mild thickening of the distal semimembranosus tendon compatible with low to moderate grade partial tearing.
Complete tear of the inferior meniscal popliteal fascicle compatible with posterior lateral corner injury.

Joint effusion: Large joint effusion.
Baker cyst: None.

Other significant findings:
None.

CONCLUSION:
*Comminuted mildly displaced avulsion fracture of the tibial spine with mild comminution, including the distal insertion of the ACL, the anterior horn root insertion of the lateral meniscus, and posterior horn root insertion zone of the medial and lateral menisci. Intra-articular fracture extension involving the central portion of the medial tibial plateau with small gap/step as described.
*Small mildly displaced lateral corner fracture of the lateral tibial plateau [Segond fracture].
*Small osteochondral impaction fracture of the lateral corner of lateral femoral condyle.
*High-grade tear of the medial collateral ligament.
*Low-grade partial tear/sprain of the anterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament.
*Additional low-grade tears involving the medial and lateral menisci as described.
*Moderate grade partial tear of the medial patellar retinaculum.
*Posteromedial and posterolateral corner injuries as described.
*Large joint effusion.

original_evidence:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: 64-year-old with progressive left knee pain related to "wear and tear". Evaluate for cartilage loss. Evaluate for meniscus tear.
Comparison: No recent left lower extremity imaging available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee is acquired in 3 anatomic planes at 1.2 Tesla using a local extremity receiver coil and a noncontrast protocol.

FINDINGS:

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Osseous and articular alignment at the left knee are normal.
No fracture. No focal osseous contusion.
No evidence for a recent pivot shift mechanism.

JOINT SPACE:
There is a small left knee effusion.
There is a minimal, partially ruptured Baker's cyst.
No intra-articular bodies.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is a complex tear of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with a dominant oblique undersurface component and a smaller inner margin radial component at the junction posterior horn and posterior root. There is moderate subsequent medial meniscus extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: There is diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss all along the weightbearing region of the medial femoral condyle, with focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the medial femoral margin.
There is partial-thickness cartilage loss at the medial tibial margin.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: The lateral meniscus shows normal morphology and signal with no tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage throughout the lateral tibiofemoral compartment is normal.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
There is a small region of focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the patellar median ridge, with more diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss extending along the medial patellar facet.
There is diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss with deep chondral fissuring at the central femoral trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal morphology and signal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): The MCL is bowed from medial meniscus extrusion, but intact.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: The fibular-collateral ligament and anterolateral ligament are normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Intact stabilizers.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Moderate degenerative hypertrophic distal quadriceps tendinopathy, with intrasubstance degeneration at its patellar attachment and mild enthesopathy. No high-grade quadriceps tear.
Patella tendon: Normal morphology and signal with no tear or degeneration.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No significant soft tissue edema in Hoffa's fat.
A TT-TG distance is normal at 7 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
The distal iliotibial band and biceps femoris are normal.
The distal semimembranosus is normal.

SOFT TISSUES:
Neurovascular structures in the popliteal fossa are normal.
Subcutaneous soft tissues are normal. No soft tissue mass.

IMPRESSION:

1. Extensive complex medial meniscus tear with a dominant oblique undersurface component at its body and posterior horn, moderate medial meniscus extrusion, and high-grade cartilage loss on the medial femoral condyle with low-grade cartilage loss at the medial tibial margin.

2. Focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the patellar median ridge with high-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss at the central femoral trochlea.

3. Moderate degenerative hypertrophic distal quadriceps tendinopathy, with mild enthesopathy.

4. Small left knee effusion with a minimal ruptured Baker's cyst.

original_evidence:
MRI ΔΕΞΙΟΥ ΓΟΝΑΤΟΣ ΤΕΧΝΙΚΗ Η εξέταση έγινε με ακολουθίες παλμών Τ1, πυκνότητας πρωτονίων με καταστολή του σήματος του λίπους και STIR. Επίσης ελήφθη ακολουθία Τ2 βαθμιδωτής ηχούς. [DATE]. ΕΥΡΗΜΑΤΑ Επανελέγχεται η κάκωση ολικής ρήξης του πρόσθιου χιαστού συνδέσμου. Επανελέγχεται βελτιούμενη σε απεικονιστικά χαρακτηριστικά η μερική κάκωση του άνω τριτημορίου του οπίσθιου χιαστού συνδέσμου. Δεν παρατηρούνται πλέον οι εστίες οστικού μώλωπα που είχαν παρατηρηθεί στην περιοχή του άπω μηριαίου και της εγγύς κνήμης. Παρατηρείται πώρωση του κατάγματος της έξω κεφαλής της περόνης με ήπια αλλοίωση της άνω επιφάνειας (malunion). Στον έξω μηριαίο κόνδυλο παρατηρείται μικρό οστικό έμφρακτο πιθανότατα δευτεροπαθώς σε παλαιότερη παρουσία οστικού μώλωπα στην περιοχή. Στον έσω μηριαίο κόνδυλο παρατηρείται μικρό κάταγμα ανεπάρκειας υπαρθρικά (συνώνυμο "αυτόματης οστεονέκρωσης") με εκτεταμένο οστικό οίδημα. Συνιστάται οστική πυκνομετρία ΟΜΣΣ. Οι αρθρικές επιφάνειες ελέγχονται ακέραιες. Ηπια τενοντοπάθεια παρατηρείται στην άνω μοίρα του επιγονατιδικού τένοντα.

Η πιθανότητα ολιγάριθµων ακέραιων ινών θεωρείται χαµηλή. - Αναγνωρίζεται διάχυτο παθολογικό σήµα µε συνοδό ασαφοποίηση της εγγύς κατάφυσης του έξω πλαγίου συνδέσµου, στο πλαίσιο µερικής ρήξης, ενώ συνυπάρχει υφολική λέπτυνση κατά τη µεσότητά του, πιθανά στο πλαίσιο υφολικής ρήξης. - Παρατηρούνται πολυάριθµες περιοχές παθολογικού σήµατος του οστικού µυελού σε αµφότερους του µηριαίους και κνηιαίους κονδύλους, στο πλαίσιο υπολειµατικού οστικού οιδήµατος. МР данни за мукоидна дегенерация на предната кръстна връзка. Връзката се проследява по цялото и протежение, но е с уголемен напречник и повишен интензитет на сигнала. Колатерални лигаменти -  б.о. Хрущялът е изтънен и е с неравни контурни очертания. Изобразяват се остеофити по кондилите на фемура, предимно от медиалната страна. Наличие на субхондрален едеме на костния мозък в медиалния фемурален кондил, във връзка с дегенеративните промени в подлежащия хрущял. Ставният хрущял от латералната страна на ставата е запазен. Визуализира се дегенеративна промяна и лезия на медиалния менискус в областта на неговия заднен рог. Задният рог на медиалният менискус е с висок интензитат на сигнала и е фрагментиран. Част от менискуса е изместен латерално от ставната междина. Дегенеративна промяна се открива и при педния рог на латералния менускус, с малка /6мм./ киста в него. Наличие на ставен излив. Кръстните връзки са интактни. Колатерални лигаменти – без особености. Сухожилие на мускулус квадрицепс феморис, лигамент на пателата – без особености Лява колянна става: Вижда се медиална гонартроза и при лявата колянна става, която е сравнително по-изразена. Ставният хрущял от медиалната страна е лизиран почти изцяло, като ставната междина е изпълнен с течност. Изобраяват се сравнително по-големи остеофитни наслагвания по феморалните кондили.  Малки остеофити се намират и по ставните краища на тибията. Наличие на субхондрален костно-мозъчен едем във феура и в тибията от медиалната страна. original_evidence:
MRI ΓΟΝΑΤΩΝ ΤΕΧΝΙΚΗ Η εξέταση έγινε µε ακολουθίες παλµών Τ1, πυκνότητας πρωτονίων µε καταστολή του σήµατος του λίπους και Τ2 βαθµιδωτής ηχούς. ∆ΕΞΙΟ ΓΟΝΑΤΟ ΕΥΡΗΜΑΤΑ Από τον έλεγχο των χιαστών και πλαγίων συνδέσµων, του έσω µηνίσκου, του αρθρικού χόνδρου σε έσω και έξω διαµέρισµα, δεν παρατηρούνται αξιόλογα ευρήµατα. Ηπια εκφύλιση χωρίς ευρήµατα ρήξης παρατηρείται στο πρόσθιο κέρας του έξω µηνίσκου. Από τον έλεγχο του εκτατικού µηχανισµού, αναγνωρίζεται λέπτυνση του αρθρικού χόνδρου στη µεσότητα και έσω αρθρική επιφάνεια της επιγονατίδος (ICRS GRADE III) µε παρουσία υπαρθρικών οστεοµυελικών βλαβών στην επιγονατίδα. Η µορφολογία συνολικά του εκτατικού µηχανισµού είναι ικανοποιητική. Ενδοαρθρικά παρατηρείται ικανή συλλογή υγρού σε επικοινωνία µε µικρή συνοβιακή κύστη Baker, παρά την έσω κεφαλή του γαστροκνηµίου µυός. Υποδορίως παρατηρούνται πολλαπλές κιρσοειδείς διευρύνσεις φλεβών. Συµπέρασµα: Εκφυλιστική οστεοαρθρίτιδα προσθίου διαµερίσµατος γόνατος µε ύδραρθρο. 

[BILATERAL NOTE: two reports filed under this study]

ΑΡΙΣΤΕΡΟ ΓΟΝΑΤΟ ΕΥΡΗΜΑΤΑ Από τον έλεγχο των µηνίσκων, των χιαστών και πλαγίων συνδέσµων και του αρθρικού χόνδρου σε έσω και έξω διαµέρισµα, δεν παρατηρούνται παθολογικά ευρήµατα. Από τον έλεγχο του εκτατικού µηχανισµού παρατηρείται συγγενής ρηχότητα της µηριαίας τροχιλίας (sulcus angle 171 ) µε ήπιο προς τα έξω το εξάρθρηµα της ο επιγονατίδας. Λέπτυνση παρουσιάζει ο αρθρικός χόνδρος της επιγονατίδας ιδίως στη µεσότητα της αρθρικής επιφάνειας (ΙCRS GRADE III) µε παρουσία υπαρθρικών οστεοµυελικών βλαβών στην επιγονατίδα. Μετρία συλλογή υγρού παρατηρείται στην άρθρωση του γόνατος σε επικοινωνία µε µικρή συνοβιακή κύστη Baker παρά την έσω κεφαλή του γαστροκνηµίου µυός. Παρατηρείται λεπτή ζώνη υγρικής συλλογής, στον προεπιγονατιδικό θύλακα. Συµπέρασµα: Εκφυλιστική οστεοαρθρίτιδα πρόσθιου διαµερίσµατος µε ύδραρθρο και προεπιγονατιδική ορογονοθυλακίτιδα.

original_evidence: SAĞ DİZ MRG. Tetkik protokolü: Çok düzlemli, çok sekanslı. Bulgular: Diz eklemini oluşturan her 3 kompartmanda santral-marjinal osteofit formasyonu izlendi.  Tibiofemoral eklem medialinde eklem aralığında daralma, ekleme komşu kemik yüzlerde subkondrial skleroz, ödem ve dejeneratif milimetrik kistler izlendi. Bu düzeyde femoral ve tibial kartilajlarda destrüksiyon izlendi. Bulgular dejeneratif artrit lehine yorumlandı. Medial menisküs diz ekleminden tamamı ile 6 mm mediale ekstrudedir. Menisküs hacminde azalma, menisküste grade III dejenerasyon ve kompleks yırtıklar izlenmektedir. Lateral menisküs diz eklem mesafesinden 5 mm laterale ekstrudedir.  Menisküs posterior horn ve gövde kesiminde bütünlük kaybı izlendi. Anterior hornda grade III dejenerasyon izlenmektedir. Anterior çapraz bağın belirgin  olarak incelmiş olduğu ve sinyalinde PD imajlarda artış olduğu izlenmektedir. Arka çapraz bağ ve lateral kollateral ligamen normaldir. Medial kollateral ligamande periligamentöz ödem izlendi.Tibiofemoral eklem lateralde periartiküler büyüğü 7 mm çaplı loose body formasyonları izlendi. original_evidence:
MRI RIGHT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Echogenic mass seen laterally in the right knee on ultrasound. Suggest for MRI evaluation.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
No prior imaging available for evaluation.

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: No definite meniscal tear, no evidence of para meniscal cyst.

Medial meniscus: Nonsurfacing hyperintensity of the posterior horn probably represents intrasubstance degeneration. No definite meniscal tear. No para meniscal cyst.

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is slightly laterally subluxed. Lateral trochlear inclination angle is borderline, measuring approximately 11 degrees. TT TG distance is not increased. Insall Salvati ratio is 1.4, which is also within normal range. Thickening of the lateral retinaculum may be due to prior subluxation. Increased fat attenuation is seen at the lateral aspect of the patella just posterior to the lateral retinaculum, may represent focal Hoffitis or secondary to postoperative change.

Fluid

Small joint effusion is seen. No loose body. Small Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Full thickness chondral loss most observable at the lateral patella facet and apex associated subchondral chondral edema. Chondral irregularity at the trochlea is also seen associated with subchondral cysts.


Medial compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Lateral compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Others:

Hoffa's fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Increasing fat signal is seen at the lateral aspect of the patella just posterior to the lateral retinaculum, may represent focal Hoffitis or secondary to postoperative change.
Otherwise no focal soft tissue mass detected at the knee.

Severe chondral loss at the patellofemoral compartment particularly involving the lateral patella facet and apex associated with marked subchondral edema and subchondral cysts at both the femoral trochlea and patella. Patella is slightly laterally subluxed with borderline lateral trochlear inclination angle but normal Insall Salvati ratio and TT TG distance.

Clinical information:
Echogenic mass seen laterally in the right knee on ultrasound. Suggest for MRI evaluation.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
No prior imaging available for evaluation.

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: No definite meniscal tear, no evidence of para meniscal cyst.

Medial meniscus: Nonsurfacing hyperintensity of the posterior horn probably represents intrasubstance degeneration. No definite meniscal tear. No para meniscal cyst.

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is slightly laterally subluxed. Lateral trochlear inclination angle is borderline, measuring approximately 11 degrees. TT TG distance is not increased. Insall Salvati ratio is 1.4, which is also within normal range. Thickening of the lateral retinaculum may be due to prior subluxation. Increased fat attenuation is seen at the lateral aspect of the patella just posterior to the lateral retinaculum, may represent focal Hoffitis or secondary to postoperative change.

Fluid

Small joint effusion is seen. No loose body. Small Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Full thickness chondral loss most observable at the lateral patella facet and apex associated subchondral chondral edema. Chondral irregularity at the trochlea is also seen associated with subchondral cysts.


Medial compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Lateral compartment: Minimal chondrosis.

Others:

Hoffa's fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Increasing fat signal is seen at the lateral aspect of the patella just posterior to the lateral retinaculum, may represent focal Hoffitis or secondary to postoperative change.
Otherwise no focal soft tissue mass detected at the knee.

Severe chondral loss at the patellofemoral compartment particularly involving the lateral patella facet and apex associated with marked subchondral edema and subchondral cysts at both the femoral trochlea and patella. Patella is slightly laterally subluxed with borderline lateral trochlear inclination angle but normal Insall Salvati ratio and TT TG distance.

original_evidence:
Na seriji MR presjeka lijevog koljena nalazi se uredna morfologija i intenziteti signala kolateralnih
ligamenata, prednjeg i stražnjeg križnog ligamenta, iliotibijalnog traktusa, patelarnog ligamenta i
tetive m. kvadricepsa.
Kompleksna flap ruptura u području korpusa i stražnjeg roga medijlanog meniska, čija se flap
komponenta prebacuje uz gornji rub stražnjeg korijena meniska.
Lateralni menisk uredne je morfologije i intenziteta signala.
Subhondralna T2 hiperintenzivna linija u srednjem dijelu medijalnog kondila femura na arealu
14x4 mm, bez okolnog koštanog edema ili lezije pripadajuće zglobne hrskavice - opisano u
smislu stabilnog osteohondritis disekansa.
Plitke fisure hrskavice obje fasete patele te medijalnog kondila femura i tibije (hondromalacija 2.
stupnja prema ICRS klasifikaciji).
Fisure pune debljine hrskavice obje fasete patele (hondromalacija 2. stupnja prema ICRS
klasifikaciji).
Ostale prikazane artikulacijske hrskavice urednih su intenziteta signala.
Minimalan izljev u koljenu. Sitna poplitealna (Bakerova) cista.
Bipartitna patela tip 3 kao anatomska varijanta.
Ostale prikazane koštane, mekotkivne i neurovaskularne strukture uredne su morfologije i
intenziteta signala.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Small joint effusion with synovitis. Large complex popliteal cyst measuring up to 65 mm with an 11 mm osseous body in the superior aspect of the cyst. Sliver of free fluid along the inferior margin of the popliteal cyst suggesting minimal recent partial rupture.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Moderate degenerative change.
Complex degenerative tear with a dominant longitudinal horizontal oblique component of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with inferior surfacing. Fraying and blunting of the meniscal free edge.
Mild thickening of the proximal MCL compatible with remote injury.
Diffuse low grade partial-thickness chondral loss. Marginal osteophytosis.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Severe degenerative change with full-thickness chondral loss of the weightbearing and posterior portion of the compartment, with subchondral reactive marrow change. Marginal osteophytosis.
Complex degenerative multidirectional tear of the posterior horn extending into the body with significant maceration and substance loss of the body and anterior and posterior horn with minimal residual meniscal substance. There is some extrusion of the body of the lateral meniscus.
Thickened popliteus insertion with intrasubstance signal compatible with moderate tendinosis
Mildly thickened lateral collateral ligament proper which could reflect the sequela of a remote injury. Mild distal biceps tendinosis.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Degenerative changes of the anterior cruciate ligament which remains intact. The PCL is intact.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Mild chondropathy. Small marginal osteophytes. Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis. Mild edema at the suprapatellar fat pad.
Scarring at that the Hoffa's fat pad which could reflect the previous surgery-for clinical correlation.

Bones:
See above.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
The intra-articular body is seen at the suprapatellar joint recess on the previous MRI is no longer present.

CONCLUSION:
1.Interval worsening of the severe osteoarthritis of the lateral compartment. Complex degenerative tearing and extensive maceration the lateral meniscus.
2.Moderate degenerative change of the medial compartment. Complex degenerative tear with a dominant longitudinal oblique tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus.
3.Mild degenerative change of the patellofemoral compartment.
4.Large complex popliteal cyst with an osseous body.

original_evidence:
MRI LEFT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Severe edema of the medial condyle of left knee.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
Prior MRI dated <[Date]> of <[Month]> <[YEAR]>

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: Nonsurfacing hyperintensity of the posterior horn probably represents intra since degeneration. No definite meniscal tear. No para meniscal cyst.

Medial meniscus: Oblique tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extension to the inferior articular surface. Findings are ready seen on prior study but appears more degenerate. Several para meniscal cysts are seen at the posterior aspect of the meniscus measuring up to 0.4 cm in size. Meniscal extrusion approximately 0.6 cm noted.

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

No joint effusion or loose body. Trace Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: A large subchondral cysts are seen at the posterior superior aspect of the tibial plateau, very much larger than prior study. Moderate degenerative changes multiple osteophytes are seen, most significant at the medial tibiofemoral joint. No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Minimal chondrosis..

Medial compartment: Focal full-thickness chondral loss measuring up to 1.3 cm in size associated subchondral edema. Moderate chondrosis in the rest of the femoral condyle Findings have slightly progressed compared to prior study.

Lateral compartment: Mild chondral irregularity. No significant subchondral edema.

Others:

Hoffas fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Oblique tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extension to the inferior articular surface, similar to previous. Interval increase in degenerative changes of the meniscus is observed. Meniscal extrusion of approximately 0.6 cm is seen. Multiple para meniscal cysts are also present.

Interval increase in degenerative changes are identified evident as shown by increased osteophytes, full-thickness chondral loss at the medial tibiofemoral joint associated increasing subchondral edema, and multiple enlarging subchondral cysts at the posterior medial tibial plateau.

[BILATERAL NOTE: report filed jointly for both studies]
The two studies are being reported together.  
Faint linear intrasubstance fluid hyperintensity is noted at the posterior horns of both menisci, in keeping with age-related persistent vascularity.  
Otherwise intact menisci, cruciate and collateral ligaments, popliteus musculotendinous units, extensor tendons and both distal iliotibial bands.  
No skeletal abnormalities of note. 
No patellofemoral dysplasia morphology demonstrated on either side.  
Well-maintained tricompartmental articular cartilage surfaces are appreciated bilaterally, with no osteochondral lesions being demonstrated.  
No knee joint effusions are present on either side, nor are there any intra-articular loose bodies. 
No anterior fat pad impingement has been demonstrated either.  
Grossly unremarkable imaged extra-articular soft tissues.

original_evidence:
MRI of right Knee with 
-SG PD FatSat, Locator, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

> The contour of PCL is not in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside on F/S T2WI, in favor of tear.
> Mild interstitial increased signal intensity of ACL, R/O grade 1 injury.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, with extending into the surface, in favor of tear.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of lateral meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of  grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to contusion.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> No evidence of bone contusion is noted.
> Increased fat stranding over infrapatellar fat pad
> Focal increased signal intenisty of patellar cartilag with fissure,in favor of grade3 patellar chondromalacia 
> Wearing of articular cartilage of rigth knee, major at medial compartment and spur formation, reflecting osteoarthritis.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar andlateral plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.

Impression: 
1. Nearly full thickness tear of PCL; differential diagnosis of high grade partial tear of PCL with ganglion cyst.
2. Tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus; R/O parameniscal cyst; differential diagnosis of  MCL bursitis.
3. Grade 1 injury of ACL.
4. C/W osteoarthritis of right knee joint and mild synovitis.
5. Infrapatellar fat pad edema.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

Conclusion: Medial and lateral meniscal tearing. Patellofemoral and lateral compartment articular cartilage degeneration also noted.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Suspected osteoarthritis/internal derangement right knee.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Diminutive appearance of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus consistent with complex tear, progressed since <[YEAR]>. Diminutive appearance of the medial meniscal body consistent with complex tear. There is peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body. The anterior horn is intact.

Intrasubstance degeneration posterior horn of the lateral meniscus without discrete tear. No lateral meniscal extrusion.

Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament without tibial translation, new since previous study. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

The medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament are intact. The fibular collateral ligament is intact. The popliteus and biceps femoris tendon attachments are intact. The interval and is intact.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No patellofemoral subluxation. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 10 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. Mild edema of the suprapatellar fat pad suggesting patellofemoral maltracking.

There is mild to moderate generalized patellofemoral chondrosis, progressed since previous study. There is extensive fissuring and thinning of medial femorotibial articular cartilage with small focal areas of full-thickness cartilage denuding, progressed since <[YEAR]>. Within the lateral formidable compartment, there is thinning of articular cartilage involving the central weightbearing aspect of the left femoral condyle and overlying the lateral tibial plateau, progressed since previous study.

Small knee joint effusion. Baker's cyst, measuring 30 x 19 x 65 mm.

Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration.

1. Progressive complex tearing of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus and progressive tricompartment chondrosis most pronounced involving the medial femorotibial compartment, consistent with progressive moderate to severe medial compartment predominant tricompartment osteoarthritis of the right knee.
2. Since <[YEAR]>, interval development of low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament without tibial translation.
3. 30 x 19 x 65 mm Baker's cyst.

Horizontal oblique tear involving the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus, extending at least 3 cm from medial to lateral with associated marked attenuation of the junction of the body and posterior horn of the meniscus and extrusion of the body of the meniscus. The medial collateral ligament appears intact.

Mild focal cartilage fissuring involving the weightbearing surface of the lateral femoral condyle without subchondral bone changes.

The lateral meniscus and fibular collateral ligament complex appear intact.

Normal.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Focal articular cartilage fissuring involving the junction of the lateral patellar facet and median ridge of the patella without subchondral bone changes.
The trochlear articular cartilage appears intact.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
1.Unstable horizontal tear involving the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with some attenuation of the junction of the body and posterior horn of the meniscus and extrusion of the body of the meniscus.
2.Associated chondrosis involving the medial femorotibial compartment, as described.
3.Patellar fissuring and chondrosis, as described.

Από τον έλεγχο του έξω διαµερίσµατος το µόνο που σηµειούται είναι παρουσία επιχείλιων οστεοφύτων. Από τον έλεγχο του πρόσθιου διαµερίσµατος παρατηρείται σηµαντική εκφυλιστική οστεοαρθρίτιδα µε διάβρωση του αρθρικού χόνδρου σε επιγονατίδα και µηριαία τροχιλία ως ICRS 4, ενώ η επιγονατίδα παρουσιάζει επίσης προς τα έξω υπεξάρθρηµα. Ενδαρθρικά παρατηρείται σηµαντική συλλογή υγρού που επικοινωνεί µε ευµεγέθη συνοβιακή κύστη Baker παρά την έσω κεφαλή του γαστροκνηµίου µυός κεφαλουραίας διαµέτρου 6cm. Εντός της αρθρικής συλλογής παρατηρούνται πολλαπλά οστεοχόνδρινα ξένα σώµατα. Σηµειούται επίσης ότι το κυαµοειδές οστό (fabella) παρουσιάζει διαµήκη διάµετρο 22mm το πιθανότερο δευτεροπαθώς στην εκφυλιστική οστεοαρθρίτιδα.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: 2 months of knee pain. Hit knee on metal bar.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small multiloculated Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal. Mild extrusion. No flipped fragments. No parameniscal cyst.
Medial compartment cartilage: Full thickness cartilage fissuring at the weightbearing medial femoral condyle with subchondral edema.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Low-grade fissuring at the lateral tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Focal high-grade fissuring at the medial facet.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 16mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. 
2.	Low-grade tricompartmental chondrosis.

original_evidence:
There is proximal non avulsive disruption of the anterior cruciate ligament, with some anteriorly displaced fragments being best appreciated in the sagittal plane.  
Marrow contusional changes are noted at the central portion of the lateral femoral condyle, also affecting the posteromedial and posterolateral tibial plateaux - the overall pattern being compatible with a pivot shift mechanism of injury.  
There is a significant resultant suprapatellar effusion with associated synovitis.  There are no convincing medial or lateral meniscal tears. A grade 1 proximal MCL injury is noted. There is furthermore a posteromedial meniscocapsular sprain. 
No posterolateral corner injury is identified, nor is there any injury to the anterolateral ligament. 
Normal PCL, lateral collateral ligament, popliteus musculotendinous unit and PTFL, distal iliotibial band and extensor tendons. Well-preserved tricompartmental hyaline articular cartilage surfaces.  
The extent of fluid signal intensity within the deep posterior soft tissues following injury suggests prior posterior capsular disruption.

original_evidence:
MRI of left Knee with 
-3-Plane Loc, Sag PD FS, Sag T2 FS, Sag T1, Ax T2 FS, Cor T2 FS

> There are linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, it extends into the surface, in favor of tear.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of lateral meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of  grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration.
> The contour of ACL & PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
> Mild heterogenous singla intensity of paterllar cartilage, in favor of grade 1-2 chondromalacia.
> Wearing of articular cartilage of left knee, major at medial compartment with spur formation and mild subchondral edema, reflecting osteoarthritis.
> Lobulated hyperintensity foci located below proximal tibiofibular joint abutting popliteal tendon/ muscle, R/O bursitis.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee with synovitis.
2. C/W tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus.
3. Grade 1-2 patellar chondromalacia.
4. R/O bursitis along popliteal tendon.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

original_evidence:
Zu [DATE] größenprogrediente Baker-Zyste mit einer cc-Ausdehnung von knapp 11 cm in lobulierter Morphologie (12/8), im kranialen Abschnitt diskontinuierlich DD rupturiert. Überwiegend diffus auslaufende Flüssigkeit im s.c. Gewebe popliteal sowie um die Unterschenkelmuskulatur. Gering Ödemsignal in den Flexoren bds. (11/32). 
Medial betonte Gonarthrose mit bekannt in der Belastungszone höhergradig gemindertem Knorpelbesatz; im Vergleich zu [DATE] dabei an der hinteren Femurkondyle Progredienz mit nun vollschichtiger Chondropathie fokal (4/23, 5/10). Zunehmende subchondrale Ödemzone des medialen Tibiaplateaus sowie der medialen Femurkondyle. Mucoide Degeneration des Innenmeniskus führend am Hinterhorn mit komplexer Rissbildung (5/9) am Übergang in die Pars intermedia aus der Voruntersuchung bekannt; der Meniskus extrudiert bei Beteiligung der Hinterwurzel. Mucoide Degeneration auch des Außenmeniskus mit möglicher, bereits vorbeschriebener Rissbildung am freien Rand. 
Fokal höhergradige Chondropathie auch lateral an der dorsolateralen Femurkondyle über 7 x 6 mm (5/26). Fokal tiefergreifende Chondropathie retropatellar sowie flächig hochgradige Chondropathie in der Trochlea mit vollschichtiger Läsion am Übergang zu den Kondylenwangen und subchondraler Reaktion/Ödembildung am Übergang zum lateralen Kompartiment (4/17). MCL-Reizzustand. Geringer Gelenkerguss mit Reizsynovialitis. Fabella. 
Kleine Baker-Zyste rechts miterfasst. Intakte Darstellung der Sehnenverläufe am Unterschenkel.

original_evidence:
FINDINGS:

Fractures:
Known mildly comminuted undisplaced avulsion fracture of the tibial tuberosity involving the distal ACL insertion, anteriorly the anterior horn root insertion of the lateral meniscus, as well as posteriorly the tibial insertion of both the posterior horn of medial and lateral menisci. The fracture involves the central portion of the medial tibial plateau articular surface anteriorly and posteriorly with articular surface collapse of 3 mm anteriorly and 5 mm posteriorly, as well as a step deformity of up to 2 mm posteriorly.
Small mildly displaced avulsion fracture of the lateral corner of lateral tibial plateau [Segond fracture].
Small mild osteochondral impaction at the anterior lateral weightbearing aspect of lateral femoral condyle.
There is associated bone marrow edema associated with these fractures.

Joint alignment:
Mild widening of the medial femorotibial joint space. Otherwise preserved articular alignment.

Degenerative changes:
None.

Bone marrow signal:
Additional small area of bone marrow edema on the medial side of medial femoral condyle without evidence of associated fracture.

Anterior cruciate ligament: The distal bony avulsion with laxity of the ACL, showing some internal high T2 signal changes compatible with additional low-grade partial ligamentous tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament: Intact with mild laxity.
Medial collateral ligament: Complete tear of the superficial portion at the mid to distal third. Moderate grade partial tear of the deep meniscal femoral and meniscal tibial components with partial meniscocapsular separation of the medial meniscal body.
Lateral collateral ligament complex: Low-grade sprain of the proximal lateral collateral ligament. The other associated structures are intact.

Medial meniscus: Mild nonspecific signal changes of the meniscal body, with evidence of small horizontal oblique tear extending to the femoral surface. No other significant tear. Bony avulsion of the posterior horn root insertion as detailed above.
Lateral meniscus: Mild nonspecific signal changes at the anterior horn compatible with low-grade tearing. Evidence of small Wrisberg rip-type longitudinal tear of the periphery of the posterior horn. Complete tear of the inferior meniscal popliteal fascicle compatible with posterior lateral corner injury. There is a bony avulsion of the anterior horn and posterior horn root insertion sites.

Extensor tendons: Normal.
Patellar retinacula: Moderate grade partial tear of the medial retinaculum.
Pes anserinus: Normal.

Posteromedial and posterolateral corner: Diffuse signal change and mild thickening of the distal semimembranosus tendon compatible with low to moderate grade partial tearing.
Complete tear of the inferior meniscal popliteal fascicle compatible with posterior lateral corner injury.

Joint effusion: Large joint effusion.
Baker cyst: None.

Other significant findings:
None.

CONCLUSION:
*Comminuted mildly displaced avulsion fracture of the tibial spine with mild comminution, including the distal insertion of the ACL, the anterior horn root insertion of the lateral meniscus, and posterior horn root insertion zone of the medial and lateral menisci. Intra-articular fracture extension involving the central portion of the medial tibial plateau with small gap/step as described.
*Small mildly displaced lateral corner fracture of the lateral tibial plateau [Segond fracture].
*Small osteochondral impaction fracture of the lateral corner of lateral femoral condyle.
*High-grade tear of the medial collateral ligament.
*Low-grade partial tear/sprain of the anterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament.
*Additional low-grade tears involving the medial and lateral menisci as described.
*Moderate grade partial tear of the medial patellar retinaculum.
*Posteromedial and posterolateral corner injuries as described.
*Large joint effusion.

ρχιτεκτονικής του χόνδρου της τροχιλίας, µε λέπτυνση και εστιακό έλλειµµα στο έξω τµήµα, καθώς και αντίστοιχα στο κεντρικό τµήµα της επιγονατίδας µε υποχόνδρινες κύστεις ισοϋψώς ( Grade II και IV αντίστοιχα).

original_evidence:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: [PROFESSION]. Right medial knee pain. 
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is a moderate, focal bone contusion/subchondral bone marrow edema at the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau at the medial joint line at the site of the medial meniscus tear. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is a complex, predominantly radial tear involving the inner margin of the body of the medial meniscus near the anterior horn/body junction (se 2, img 20 and se 5, img 11) with a superiorly flipped thin fragment extending into the anteromedial meniscofemoral recess (se 5, img 12 to 16 and se 4, img 7). Underlying reactive bone marrow edema at the medial femoral condyle and to a lesser degree at the medial tibial plateau. The tear of the meniscal body slightly extends into the posterior horn. No significant meniscal extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There are small 3 mm areas of focal full thickness cartilage fissuring (grade 4 chondral fissuring) at the medial patellar facet and at the groove of the femoral trochlea. 

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 3 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Complex, predominantly radial tear involving the inner margin of the body of the medial meniscus with a superiorly flipped meniscal fragment extending into the meniscofemoral recess. 
2.	Moderate, focal bone contusion/subchondral bone marrow edema at the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau at the medial joint line at the site of the medial meniscus tear. 
3.	Patellofemoral compartment: Small 3 mm areas of focal full thickness cartilage fissuring (grade 4 chondral fissuring) at the medial patellar facet and at the groove of the femoral trochlea. 
4.	Moderate knee joint effusion.

МР находка: Дясна колянна става: Няма МР данни за ставен излив. Костите, формиращи колянната става са със запазена форма. Виждат се остеофитни наслоявания на пателата – супратрохлеарно вляво, като същата е сублуксирана в латерално направление. Ставният хрущял на фемуропателарната става е изтънен с наличие на ерозии на хрущяла на пателата и малки субхондрални костни кисти по задния и ръб с перифокален едем по съседство. Дефект с кос ход, на късо протежение в хрущяла на медиалния кондил на десния фемур в зоната на максимално натоварване, без подлежаща субхондрална костна лезия. Субхондрални костни кисти „геоди“ се изобразяват под интеркондиларните еминенции, които са изострени. Подобни малки кисти се виждат и на нивото на тибиофибуларната става.  Нормално изобразяване на кръстните връзки. Визуализират се дегенеративни промени в задния рог на медиалния менискус. Нормално изобразяване на латералния менискус. Колатерални лигаменти – нормално изобразяване. Лигамент на пателата, сухожилие на м. квадрицепс феморис – без особености. Поплитеална ямка – б.о. Лява колянна става: Състояние след парциална менискектомия и остеохондропластика [DATE]г. 
МР данни за начални дегенеративни промени в лявата колянна става. Визуализират се малки остеофити по ставните краища на фемура и тибията, предимно на медиалните кондили.  Интеркондиларните еминенции са изострени. Наличие на остеохондрален дефект в предната половина на медиалния кондил на фемура с обширен костномозъчен едем, извън зоната на максимално натоварване. Вижда се дефект в подлежащия ставен хрущял на това ниво. В останалите си отдели артикулиращият ставен хрущял на на тибията и фемура е със запазена конгруентност, лекостепенно изтънен.  Предната кръстна връзка е със запазена цялост. Задна кръстна връзка – б.о. Нормално изобразяване на латералния менискус при начални дегенеративни промени в задния му рог. Визуализира се руптура с хоризонтален към кос ход в задния рог на медиалния менискус – степен 2b. Колатерални лигаменти - нормално изобразяване на медиалния колатерален лигамент. Дегенеративни промени в залавните места на латералния колатерален лигамент, който е със запазена цялост.  Пателата е с белези на хондрмалация. Вижда се малък дефект срединно в хрущяла на ставния хрущял в областта на горния полюс в съчетание с едемни субхондрални промени в прилежащата задна стена на пателата. Находката съответства на ходромалация – IV степен по Outerbridge grading system. Ретинакулуми – б.о. Нормално изобразяване на меките тъкани. Заключение: Дясна колянна става: МР данни за трохлеарна дисплазия – тип В по Dejour. Латерална сублуксация на пателата. Начални гонартрозни промени с хондромалация на пателата.

Лява колянна става: МР данни за гонартроза. Остеохондрален дефект в медиален кондил на фемура. Хондромалация на пателата -  IV степен по Outerbridge. Лезия в задния рог на медиалния менискус – 2b степен.

original_evidence:
Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Pain in the left kidney; right knee pain for 4 weeks, no injury.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. 

JOINT SPACE:
Trace joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Cartilage heterogeneity and fissuring along the weightbearing lateral tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Full-thickness fissuring at the junction of the median ridge/lateral patellar facet with subchondral edema.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: Mild patellar tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 7 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Lateral and patellofemoral compartment chondrosis.
2.	Mild patellar tendinosis without tear.

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    ? Anterior cruciate ligament   .

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact. Patellofemoral ligaments are intact and unremarkable. Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is well-maintained. The TT-TG distance is within normal limits.

There is a complex bucket-handle tear of medial meniscus. Fragments are seen. Into the intercondylar notch there is associated chondral fraying seen to the weightbearing cartilage of the medial femoral condyle as well as the tibial cartilage to a lesser degree.

There is a linear tear seen in the posterior horn and posterior body of lateral meniscus extending to the inferior articular surface with some apical truncation. There is a disruption of the lateral meniscal tibial ligament with superior displacement of the meniscal body away from the tibial plateau. No other meniscal tear is seen to the lateral meniscus. There is severe chondral thinning and fissuring and fraying seen to the weightbearing cartilage of lateral femoral condyle and to a lesser degree lateral tibial plateau.

There are no normal intact anterior cruciate ligament fibers demonstrated. There is heterogeneous thickened mixed T2 signal seen along the course of the anterior cruciate ligament. Findings are in keeping with a high-grade to complete anterior cruciate ligament tear. There is an associated anterior cruciate ligament ganglion cyst. Anterior tibial drawer measured in the lateral joint compartment is between 5 and 6 mm is borderline.

The posterior cruciate ligament is intact and appears unremarkable.

The medial collateral ligament is intact and appears unremarkable.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including the fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon, popliteus tendon and IT band all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a small Baker's cyst demonstrated.

There is a moderate knee effusion with mild reactive synovitis.

INTERPRETATION: 

Bucket-handle tear of medial meniscus with moderate chondrosis to the medial joint compartment.

Complex tear of lateral meniscus involving body and posterior horn associated with what appears to be disruption of the meniscotibial attachment laterally. Severe chondrosis is seen to the lateral joint compartment.

High-grade to complete subacute to nonacute tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with anterior cruciate ligament ganglion cyst. Borderline anterior tibial drawer.

Moderate Baker's cyst.

Large knee effusion with synovitis.

Στον υποδόριο ιστό καθώς και ενδοµυϊκά παρατηρούνται κιρσοειδή φλεβικά αγγεία. Συµπέρασµα: Εξέταση χωρίς αξιόλογα παθολογικά ευρήµατα.

original_evidence:
Antecedentes Clínicos:
Tendinitis rotuliana bilateral.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones en significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios de rotura.
Condropatía superficial de la zona de carga de los compartimentos femorotibiales y de la rótula.
Cartílago troclear sin alteraciones.
No hay derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Engrosamiento y aumento de señal del tercio proximal del tendón rotuliano con pequeña rotura
intrasustancia de sus fibras centrales que mide 4 x 3 mm con un componente delaminativos
intrasustancia de 6 mm. Esto se asocia a mínimo edema óseo y edema de la grasa de Hoffa.
Tendón cuadricipital, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de
límites normales.
Impresión:
Tendinosis rotuliana proximal con pequeña rotura parcial intrasustancia, asociado a edema óseo
del aspecto inferior de la rótula y de la grasa de Hoffa adyacente.
Condropatía superficial de la zona de carga de los compartimentos femorotibiales y de la rótula

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Small joint effusion. Small ganglion cyst on the undersurface of the medial gastrocnemius muscle, measuring 0.8 x 0.3 cm. No popliteal cyst.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Small peripheral oblique tear at the posterior inferior corner of the medial meniscus at the junction of the body and posterior horn. There is a mild sprain of the medial collateral ligament with superficial edema.. Cartilage is preserved.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Lateral meniscus, cartilage and lateral collateral ligament complex are intact.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Normal.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Sequela of recent lateral patellar dislocation (reduced). Associated impaction fracture of the lateral femoral condyle peripherally with extensive bone marrow edema, and an additional osteochondral impaction involving the medial patellar facet with bone marrow edema and articular depression. There is adjacent soft tissue edema.
The adjacent patellar attachment of the medial patellofemoral ligament demonstrates is severe edema and irregularity suggestive of significant partial thickness injury. Insall-Salvati ratio and tibial tuberosity-trochlea groove (TT-TG) distance are within normal limits. Hypoplastic medial trochlear facet with increased angulation of the lateral trochlear facet.
Mild thickening of the medial patellar plica.

Bones:
As above.


Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

Sequela of recent lateral patellofemoral dislocation (now reduced), with osteochondral impaction of the medial patellar facet and impaction fracture lateral femoral condyle, with extensive bone marrow edema. No displaced osteochondral loose body.

Significant injury to the adjacent patellar attachment of the medial patellar femoral ligament.

Associated low-grade sprain of the medial collateral ligament.

Altered morphology of the trochlea with hypoplastic medial facet and increased angulation of the lateral facet.

Suspect small peripheral inferior corner oblique tear at the junction of the body and posterior horn medial meniscus.
